# Carson Poore Consulting

> A growth consultancy in Indianapolis, Indiana with four practices (marketing, technical, strategy, and coaching) for local small businesses, founders, and nonprofits. Prices are published on the site: monthly retainers at $1,200, $2,400, or $4,800, a $3,000 one-time strategy engagement (half credited toward a retainer if the client continues), and a reduced nonprofit rate. Eight clients at a time across all engagements, a three-month minimum then month to month, and clients keep everything (site, Google Business Profile, ad accounts, data) if they leave. Serves Indianapolis and central Indiana locally; technical and coaching work nationwide. Contact: carson@carsonpoore.com.

## Practices

- [Marketing](https://carsonpoore.com/services/marketing): Brand, campaigns, content, and email measured in calls, customers, and booked work.
- [Technical](https://carsonpoore.com/services/technical): AI agents and automation, websites and web apps, GoHighLevel and CRM, Google Ads, and GA4, priced for small businesses.
- [Strategy & planning](https://carsonpoore.com/services/strategy): A $3,000 one-time engagement covering positioning, ideal customer, offer, and a 90-day plan the client keeps; $1,500 is credited toward a retainer if the client continues.
- [Coaching & growth](https://carsonpoore.com/services/coaching): Fractional CMO and marketing advisory at $1,200 to $4,800 a month, with the plan and the hands on one team.

## Services

- [Branding](https://carsonpoore.com/services/branding): Logo and identity from $750; full brand system (identity, brand voice, guidelines) from $2,000. Positioning comes from the strategy engagement.
- [Content marketing](https://carsonpoore.com/services/content-marketing): Articles that answer customer questions, email newsletters, and guides, run inside the monthly retainers.
- [Social media](https://carsonpoore.com/services/social-media): Planning, posting, short-form video, and replies on the platforms customers use, run inside the monthly retainers.
- [Video & photo](https://carsonpoore.com/services/video-photo): Intro video from $1,200, short-form video pack (6 vertical videos) from $750, half-day photo shoot from $500, shot on location in central Indiana.
- [SEO & AI search](https://carsonpoore.com/services/seo): Technical foundations, answer-first pages, structured data, and getting found in Google and AI answers; runs inside the monthly retainers.
- [Local SEO](https://carsonpoore.com/services/local-seo): Google Business Profile, reviews, and local search visibility in Indianapolis and central Indiana.
- [Google Ads management](https://carsonpoore.com/services/google-ads): Search ads with tracking set up first; the client owns the account and the leads.
- [Web design & development](https://carsonpoore.com/services/websites): Fast small-business websites and web apps the client fully owns.
- [AI agents & automation](https://carsonpoore.com/services/ai-automation): Practical automation for small businesses, with a human approving what goes out.
- [GoHighLevel & CRM](https://carsonpoore.com/services/crm-gohighlevel): GoHighLevel setup, migration, pipelines, and follow-up automation.
- [GA4 & analytics](https://carsonpoore.com/services/analytics): GA4 cleanup, conversion and call tracking, and monthly reports a person can read.
- [Google Ad Grants](https://carsonpoore.com/services/google-ad-grants): Management of Google's $10,000/month in-kind search ads program for eligible nonprofits.

## Who we help

- [Local businesses](https://carsonpoore.com/for/local-businesses): Trades, home services, restaurants, retail, and salons in central Indiana.
- [Founders & startups](https://carsonpoore.com/for/founders): Strategy engagement first, then fractional CMO support and technical builds.
- [Nonprofits](https://carsonpoore.com/for/nonprofits): Ad Grants, donor CRM and email, storytelling, and board-ready reporting at a reduced rate.

## Pricing and method

- [You keep everything](https://carsonpoore.com/ownership): What clients own (domain, site, Google profile, ad accounts, data) and how leaving works.
- [Pricing](https://carsonpoore.com/investment): All published prices, terms, and what every retainer includes.
- [Project pricing](https://carsonpoore.com/investment#projects): Starting prices for one-time projects: starter website from $900, business site from $2,500, simple web tool from $6,000 (larger custom web apps quoted per project), logo and identity from $750, full brand system from $2,000, intro video from $1,200, short-form video pack from $750, half-day photo shoot from $500.
- [The method](https://carsonpoore.com/method): Five steps: Conviction, Your people, A sharp offer, The experience, Word of mouth.
- [About](https://carsonpoore.com/about): Founder Carson Poore, mission, vision, and values.

## Articles

- [Article library](https://carsonpoore.com/articles): All articles, sorted by topic.
- [How to get more Google reviews, within Google’s rules](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/how-to-get-more-google-reviews): Text every customer your direct review link the day the job wraps. Ask everyone, offer nothing, never screen. The routine, a copy-ready text, and the rules.
- [Google Business Profile optimization checklist (2026)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/google-business-profile-optimization): A Google Business Profile optimization checklist for local owners: category, name, hours, description, services, photos, and posts. Free, and about an hour.
- [Local SEO in Indianapolis: what Indy businesses should do](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/local-seo-indianapolis): Local SEO in Indianapolis comes down to relevance, distance, and prominence. What to fix first, how Carmel, Fishers, and Greenwood differ, and what it costs.
- [How much does a small business website cost in 2026?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/small-business-website-cost): Next to nothing up front on a DIY builder, about $300–$6,000 hired out, and under $10,000 at most agencies. Plus the ongoing costs, and when to skip it.
- [How much do Google Ads cost a small business? (2026)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/google-ads-cost-small-business): Most local businesses pay $2 to $10 a click and $27 to $132 a lead. What $1,000 a month buys, how to set a budget from job value, and who should wait.
- [Google Ads vs Facebook Ads for a local business (2026)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/google-ads-vs-facebook-ads): Google catches people already searching; Facebook interrupts people scrolling. 2026 cost-per-lead benchmarks, which fits your business, and when to skip both.
- [How to get your business recommended by ChatGPT (2026)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/get-recommended-by-chatgpt): Nobody can guarantee it. What raises your odds: a complete Google profile, recent reviews, matching listings, Bing indexing, and pages that answer first.
- [Do your own marketing or hire someone? A simple test](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/diy-marketing-vs-hiring): Do it yourself with 5 steady hours a week and a clear customer. Hire when hours run out or the work needs a skill you lack. A test by time, skill, and stakes.
- [Email marketing for small business: how often to send](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/small-business-email-marketing): Send at least once a month, twice if you have news worth sharing. What to write, how to build a list, and the Gmail and Yahoo rules to follow. Real data.
- [How often should a small business post on social media?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/how-often-to-post-on-social-media): Plan 3 to 5 posts a week on Instagram and 2 to 5 on LinkedIn. Per-platform numbers from Buffer and Sprout, and why steady beats busy for a small shop.
- [Is blogging still worth it for small business in 2026?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/does-blogging-still-work): Sometimes. AI Overviews cut clicks, but business websites are still the biggest source AI tools cite. When a small-business blog pays off and when to skip it.
- [GA4 setup for small business: what to turn on and read](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/ga4-for-small-business): Set up GA4 in an afternoon: mark key events, read Traffic acquisition and Landing page, and avoid the setup mistakes that skew small-business numbers.
- [Best CRM for small business: picks by business type](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/best-crm-for-small-business): Pick a CRM by the job it does, not the feature list. Honest picks for service, sales, and solo owners with verified October 2026 prices and who should skip one.
- [GoHighLevel vs HubSpot: real costs and who each fits](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/gohighlevel-vs-hubspot): GoHighLevel is $97 a month flat; HubSpot Professional starts at $890. The head-to-head, costs at 1,000, 5,000, and 10,000 contacts, and who should pick each.
- [How to automate lead follow-up (and keep a human in it)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/automate-lead-follow-up): Automate the first reply and reminders, keep a person on the conversation. A six-touch, 7-day sequence, sourced speed-to-lead stats, and texting rules.
- [Is an AI chatbot worth it for a small business website?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/ai-chatbot-for-website): Sometimes. It pays off when visitors repeat the same questions and a person can take over fast. Costs, real failures, handoff rules, and who should skip it.
- [Website redesign vs. refresh: which does your site need?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/website-redesign-or-refresh): Refresh if the site still says what you do and works on a phone. Redesign only when the foundation blocks you. A decision table, costs, and what to fix first.
- [How to write a one-page marketing plan (free template)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/one-page-marketing-plan): Write it on one page with six boxes: a goal with a number and date, your best customer, your offer, two channels, a weekly rhythm, and a check. Template inside.
- [How to measure marketing ROI for a small business](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/measure-marketing-roi): One formula, two numbers to track, and an honest look at attribution. How to count calls and booked jobs, and when tracking isn't worth the trouble.
- [How to market a startup with no budget (2026 guide)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/startup-go-to-market-no-budget): Talk to 10 people with the problem, write one sentence on who it’s for, then win your first customers by hand. What to skip, what’s free, and when to get help.
- [Why isn’t my website getting leads? 5 fixable causes](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/website-not-getting-leads): Either too few people arrive or the ones who do don’t act. Five fixable causes, each with a quick self-check, starting with how to tell which problem you have.
- [When to hire a fractional CMO (and when to wait)](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/when-to-hire-fractional-cmo): Hire a fractional CMO when customers buy, revenue is real, and nobody owns marketing. Wait if people aren't buying yet. Signs by stage, and when to skip.
- [How much does a marketing consultant cost in 2026?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/marketing-consultant-cost): Marketing consultants charge about $75 to $300 an hour, $5,000 to $50,000 a project, or $1,500 to $15,000 a month. Here's what drives it, and our prices.
- [Nonprofit marketing on a small budget: 5 moves that work](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/nonprofit-marketing-small-budget): Start with what’s free: Google’s Ad Grant, free Workspace and Canva, a monthly donor email, fast thank-yous, volunteers, and one local partner. Costs and time.
- [What does a fractional CMO cost?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/fractional-cmo-cost): 2026 market ranges with sources, plus CPC's published rates.
- [Fractional CMO vs. marketing agency](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/fractional-cmo-vs-marketing-agency): Senior judgment vs. production capacity, and when each wins.
- [Is GoHighLevel worth it?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/is-gohighlevel-worth-it): Real running costs and who should skip it.
- [How to use AI agents in a small business](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/ai-agents-for-small-business): Start with one repeated task and keep a human approving.
- [Why isn't my business showing up on Google?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/not-showing-up-on-google): Five fixable causes with free self-checks.
- [How much should a small business spend on marketing?](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/small-business-marketing-budget): The common 7–8% guideline with dollar tables.
- [Google Ad Grants for nonprofits](https://carsonpoore.com/articles/nonprofit-google-ad-grant): Eligibility, compliance rules, and keeping the grant active.
